cards.text: This happens in the first year of Belshazzar, king of Babylon. Daniel, an exile from Judah, has a dream as he lies on his bed, and when visions pass through his mind, he writes the dream down. Friend, my dreams are GONE before the oven's even warm.
Daniel says, "In my vision in the night I looked, and suddenly the four winds of heaven were churning up the great sea." The four winds of heaven, friend, and the great sea is CHURNING.

cards.question: The four winds of heaven are churning up the great sea in Daniel's vision. What comes up out of it?
The four great beasts that come up out of the sea all look alike.

cards.text: The first beast is like a lion, and it has the wings of an eagle. A lion with WINGS, friend, and I can't even hop without my gold base coming along.

cards.question: Daniel keeps watching the beast that's like a lion. What happens to its eagle wings?
With its wings gone, the lion-like beast is lifted from the ground, made to stand on two feet and given the mind of a ___.

cards.text: Then another beast shows up that looks like a bear, raised up on one of its sides. It has three ribs in its mouth between its teeth, which is my mustache after I taste-test a batch, only mine is crumbs.

cards.question: The bear-like beast has three ribs in its mouth. What is it told to do?

answers.text: Get up and gorge on flesh
Go back down into the sea

cards.text: Next comes a beast like a leopard, with four wings like a bird's on its back. And FOUR heads, when I've got one head and still can't remember where I set the timer.

cards.question: The leopard-like beast is given authority to rule.

cards.text: Then a fourth beast appears, terrifying, dreadful and extremely strong, with large iron teeth. Daniel doesn't even say it's like any animal, friend. It's just NOPE.

cards.question: The fourth beast devours and crushes with its iron teeth. What does it do with whatever is left?

answers.text: Leaves it for the other beasts

cards.question: The fourth beast is a lot like the three beasts that came before it.

cards.text: This beast has ten horns, and while Daniel is thinking about them, a little horn comes up among them. He's still counting horns, and here comes ANOTHER one.

cards.question: When the little horn comes up among the ten horns, what happens to three of the first horns?
This little horn has eyes like those of a man and a mouth that speaks words of ___.

cards.text: As Daniel keeps watching, thrones are set in place and the Ancient of Days takes His seat. His clothing is white as snow, the hair of His head is like pure wool, and His throne is flaming with fire, its wheels all ablaze.

cards.question: A river of fire flows out from the presence of the Ancient of Days.
A crowd attends the Ancient of Days and stands before Him. How many are there?

cards.text: The court is convened, and the books are opened. I spent years in a junk drawer holding my breath every time that thing opened, and friend, I'd be holding it right now too.

cards.question: Daniel keeps watching because of the arrogant words the horn is speaking. What happens to the beast?

answers.text: It's slain and thrown into the fire
It flees back into the great sea
It bows down before the throne

cards.question: The rest of the beasts lose their dominion, but they're allowed to live on for a season and a time.

cards.text: Then Daniel says, "I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven." He approaches the Ancient of Days and is led into His presence.

cards.question: One like the Son of Man is led into the presence of the Ancient of Days. What kind of kingdom is He given?

answers.text: One that will never be destroyed
One that lasts for a season
One that is shared with the beasts

cards.question: One like the Son of Man is given dominion, glory and kingship, so that the people of every nation and language should ___ Him.

cards.text: And Daniel? He's grieved in his spirit, and the visions alarm him. Friend, I get alarmed when the oven timer goes off and I forgot I even SET it.

cards.question: Daniel is alarmed by everything he's seen. What does he do about it?

answers.text: Asks someone standing there what it means
Calls for the wise men of Babylon

cards.text: One of those standing there gives him the interpretation. The four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.

cards.question: These four kings will receive the kingdom and possess it forever.
Instead, the ___ of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever.

cards.text: But Daniel wants to know the true meaning of the fourth beast, the terrifying one that's different from all the others. Now we find out it has bronze claws too, because apparently iron teeth weren't ENOUGH.

He also wants to know about the ten horns, and the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell. That's the one with eyes, a mouth that spoke words of arrogance, and an appearance more imposing than the others.

cards.question: As Daniel watches, the arrogant horn is waging war. Who is it fighting against?

answers.text: The rest of the ten horns

cards.question: In this war, the horn is prevailing against the saints.

cards.text: But that goes on only until the Ancient of Days arrives and pronounces judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High. UNTIL, friend. Best word in the whole sentence.

cards.question: Once the Ancient of Days judges in favor of the saints, the time comes for them to ___ the kingdom.

cards.text: Then the one standing there explains: the fourth beast is a fourth kingdom, different from all the other kingdoms. It will devour the whole earth, trample it down and crush it.

cards.question: The fourth beast is a kingdom. What are the ten horns on its head?

answers.text: Ten kings who rise from it

cards.question: After the ten kings, another king rises, different from the earlier ones, and he subdues all ten of them.

cards.text: This king will speak out against the Most High and oppress the saints of the Most High. He'll be intending to change the appointed times and laws.

cards.question: The saints will be given into this king's hand. For how long?

answers.text: A time and times and half a time
Seventy years in a foreign land

cards.text: But the court will convene, the same court Daniel saw in his vision with the books opened.

cards.question: When the court convenes, what happens to this king's dominion?

answers.text: It's taken away and destroyed forever
It's handed over to another king
It's extended for one more season

cards.question: The kingdom given to the saints of the Most High will last only for a season.

cards.text: Daniel says, "Thus ends the matter." But his thoughts trouble him greatly, and friend, after a night like that, I bet he didn't hit snooze.

cards.question: Daniel's thoughts trouble him so greatly that his face turns ___.
After all of this, what does Daniel do with the matter?

findings.problem: The card calls Daniel 'an exile from Judah.' That fact comes from outside the passage (Daniel 1:1-6). The card gives no reference for it, and its citation covers only Daniel 7:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'when visions pass through his mind, he writes the dream down' ties the writing to the moment of the visions. The text says the visions passed through his mind as he lay on his bed, and then says separately that he wrote the dream down. It never says when he wrote it.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: After the quote, Papa Dorin's line ('The four winds of heaven, friend, and the great sea is CHURNING.') just repeats the verse with emphasis. It has no reaction, comparison or laugh. It reads as filler, not as Papa Dorin being funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question treats two groups as one crowd: 'attends the Ancient of Days and stands before Him.' The right answer, 'Thousands upon thousands,' is true only for those who attended Him. The text says 'myriads upon myriads stood before Him' (Daniel 7:10).

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: 'What happens to the beast?' doesn't say which beast. Four beasts are in the vision, and the text means the fourth beast, the one with the arrogant horn.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Instead,' which points back to the true or false statement on card 13. That card is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The saints' (2 words), is much shorter than the wrong answers, 'The other three beasts' and 'The rest of the ten horns.' That makes it stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The Ancient of Days appears for the first time and isn't identified. papa-dorin.md says to say who a new person is the first time they show up. Daniel 7 never names the Ancient of Days as God, though, and the Scripture rules say to leave open what the text leaves open.
findings.question: In a vision, should Papa Dorin identify the Ancient of Days as God the first time He appears, or leave the title as the text gives it?

findings.problem: One like the Son of Man appears and isn't identified. Daniel 7 doesn't say who He is. Jesus applies this verse to Himself (Mark 14:62), and Papa Dorin's backstory is centered on Jesus, the Lamb. The docs don't say whether Prep should make that connection, with a reference, or leave the figure unnamed.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin connect One like the Son of Man to Jesus here, citing a passage like Mark 14:62, or tell only what Daniel 7 says?
